name: Programmed freezing of Tris-egg-yolk-glycerol bull semen in 0.5 mL straws (5 to -140 °C at 5/40/20 °C/min, Mini Digitcool UJ400) with plunge into liquid nitrogen
plain_name: Freeze bull semen straws for artificial insemination in a programmable freezer
description: USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program protocol: bull semen extended in Tris-egg yolk (final 7% glycerol) is cooled to 5 °C over 2 h, loaded into 0.5 mL straws and frozen in a programmable freezer on a three-segment curve (5 to -10 °C at 5 °C/min, -10 to -110 °C at 40 °C/min, -110 to -140 °C at 20 °C/min), then plunged into liquid nitrogen for storage and later thawed 30 s at 37 °C for artificial insemination of cattle.
keywords: Freeze bull semen straws for artificial insemination in a programmable freezer

sources.citation: USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program: Bull Semen Collection, Transportation, Processing and Cryopreservation Protocol (P. Purdy; created May 2015, modified April 2020)

reported_equipment: Cryo Bio System Mini Digitcool UJ400 (IMV Corporation, Minneapolis, MN)

requirements.rationale: The freezing curve starts at 5 °C (278.15 K) and ends at -140 °C (133.15 K) inside the freezer chamber before the plunge, so the chamber must control temperature across that whole span.
The curve uses controlled cooling rates of 5, 40 and 20 °C/min, so the freezer must impose rates from 5 °C/min (5000 mK/min) to 40 °C/min (40000 mK/min).
At -140 °C the straws are plunged into liquid nitrogen for storage; liquid nitrogen must be available at the freezer.
The method is a programmed, controlled-rate freeze; the core temperature and rate keys already decide most machines, so this documented-process flag is supporting only.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
